status: unpublished source; native workerd/R2 finalization and retention checks passed; no runtime release or deployment

baseline.observed: Program returned 42 with empty stderr, but reading its buffered UTF-8 file through the real service binding returned empty content.

ownership.nativeLifecycle: State.finish flushes before output capture/serialization and Step.Done. Only non-retained filesystem executions enable the pass.
ownership.streamDiscovery: Pinned RustPython GcInterpreterState.get_objects(None) supplies this interpreter objects across ordinary and permanent generations; original native _IOBase type is captured at initialization. No stream registry or strong-reference lifetime is added.
ownership.suspension: Flush calls remain inside the same poll export and existing Asyncify request/response path; existing fuel, request count, memory, authority and deadline limits remain in force.
ownership.failure: Closed streams are skipped. ValueError while reading an unusable closed state is skipped for partially initialized/detached native objects. Errors from flush itself stop the pass, report the original exception, return null result and exit code 1.
ownership.retention: Retained contexts disable finishing flush, keeping buffers and file state in their existing native R2 heap.

coverage: Buffered UTF-8 data persists before a normal return becomes visible
Native BufferedWriter over FileIO constructed directly after io setup flushes without an open-wrapper registry
Cyclic references and gc.freeze permanent-generation objects remain discoverable
A reported Python exception retains its original diagnostic and persists buffered file data
A closed underlying descriptor causes nonzero completion with null result, original EBADF diagnostic and no committed pending bytes
An uninitialized BufferedWriter does not prevent another live writer from flushing
Existing retained-writer test still sees only explicitly flushed bytes between entries, preserves denied buffers and resumes under current grants

microbenchmark.scope: Same final native Wasm; finalization enabled versus disabled; excludes construction, begin, R2/workerd and production

microbenchmarkSummary.measurement: Eight phases ABBA/BAAB, one warmup then four measured steps each. Same final Wasm, filesystem enabled in both variants, source 1+1, unchanged one-million instruction ceiling. All results equal 2. Timing includes native step and result decoding; excludes construction/begin, workerd, R2 and production.
microbenchmarkSummary.scopeLimit: Tiny no-file native workload only; not a production latency, cold start, R2 billing or AgentOS comparison.

limits: This is a buffered-stream flush pass, not full interpreter finalization, atexit or arbitrary user-defined shutdown support
Native traps, interruption and interop failures do not force borrowed interpreter cleanup
Writes after the final unlink, full cross-context detached-inode coherence, eager io.FileIO setup and remaining stdlib/pip remain open
Existing Python heaps require explicit reset when adopting this different binary; no replay or automatic conversion
No remote deployment or production performance/cost claim
